body.text: THE ARGVMENT OF THE BOOKE
OF GENESIS.
THIS firſt Booke of holie Sripture, called Geneſis, which ſignifieth
birth or beginning, was written by Moyſes, when he was deſigned by
God, to inſtruct & rule the children of Iſrael. As also the other foure bookes
folowing. The Author and authoritie of al which fiue bookes, were euer
acknowledged by the faithful, both of the old and new Teſtament: and ſo
accounted and eſtemed by tradition, i.⟨e?⟩ Chriſt and his Apoſtles: who alſo
confirmed them by their teſtimonies, and allegations of the ſame, as of holie
Scriptures. From the creation vntil Moyſes writ (which was aboue two thou-
ſand and foure hundred yeares) the Church exerciſed Religion by Reuelati-
ons made to certaine Patriarches, and by Traditions from man to man, with-
out anie Scriptures or Law written. But the peculiar people of God being
more viſibly ſeparated from other nations, & manie errors abunding in the
world, God would for correction & confuſation therof, haue his wil made
further knowen to his children, and ſo remaine amongſt them in written
record, by his faithful ſeruant and Prophet Moyſes. VVho therfore declareth
the Author and beginning of al thinges, that is, How al creatures were
made by God, and of him haue their being, and by him only are conſerued.
He teacheth expreſly that there is one onlie God, againſt thoſe that imagi-
ned and brought into the phantaſies of men manie goddes. That the whole
or vniuerſal ſubſtance of heauen and earth, with their ornaments and acci-
dents, were made in time; againſt thoſe that thought the firſt fundation ther-
of had euer benne. That God doth gouerne the ſame; againſt thoſe that ſay,
al is ruled by deſtenie or by the ſtarres, and not by the continual prouidence
of God. That God is a rewarder of the good, and a puniſher of euil; which
ſinners ſeme either not to know, or groſly to forgete. And that God created
al for mans vſe and benefite, which should make vs grateful. VVherfore
holie Moyſes more particularly deſcribeth the beginning of man; what he was
at firſt; how he fel; how al mankind is come of one man: deducing the
Genealogie of Adam, especially to Noe. Then how men being more and
more defiled vpon the earth, with wicked, especially carnal ſinnes, were by
Gods iuſt wrath drowned with an vniuerſal floud.
Againe how a few reſerued perſons multiplied the world anew. But
this ofſpring alſo falling into manie ſinnes, especially Idolatrie and ſpiri-
tual fornication, as thoſe of the firſt age did to carnal offences, God ſtil con-
ſerued ſome faithful & true ſeruants. Of which Moyſes ſpecially purſueth
the line of Noe by Sem his firſt begotten ſonne. Then deſcribeth the particular
vocations, liues, maners, notable ſayings, and noble factes, with ſincere re-
ligion of Abraham, Iſaac, Iacob, Ioſeph, & other holie Patriarches: who
liued before the vvritten lavv. Likevviſe vpon VVhat occaſion, & in vvhat
maner,
THE ARGVMENT OF GENESIS.
maner, Iacob otherwiſe called Iſrael, with al his progenie, deſcended from
the Land of Canaan into Ægypt, and were there entertayned. So this booke
contayneth the hiſtorie of two thouſand three hundred & odde yeares. And
it may be diuided into eight partes. The firſt contayneth the Creation of
Heauen and Earth, & other Creatures, and laſtly of Man. chap. 1. & 2.
The ſecond part is of the trangreſſion & fal of man, & his caſting out
Paradiſe, of multiplication of men, and of ſinne, though ſtil ſome were
iuſt, of the general floud, that drowned al except eight perſons, & few other
liuing creatures of the earth. from the third chap. to the 8. The third part is
of the new increaſe, & multiplication of the ſame. from the 8. chap. to
11. The fourth, of the confuſion of tongues, & the diuiſion of nations. in
the 11. chap. The fift relateth Abrahams going forth of his countrie, Gods
promiſe, that in his ſeede al Nations should be bleſſed, & the commandment
of Circumciſion, from the 12. chap. to the 21. The ſixth part recounteth
progenie, and other bleſſings, especially the great vertues of Abraham, Iſaac,
and Iacob. from the 21. chap. to the 37. The ſeuenth part reporteth the ſel-
ling of Ioſeph into Ægypt, and his aduancement there. from the 37. chap. to
the 46. The eight and laſt part is of Iacob, and his progenies going into
Ægypt, their intertainment there, and of Iacobs, and finally of Ioſephs
death. in the fiue laſt cahpters.

uncertain.note: PRESERVED PRINTER'S TYPO for 'Scripture' (medial 'c' dropped). Confirmed at 4x zoom vs the correctly-spelled 'Scriptures' at line_index 8 and 'Scriptures' line_index 12. Diplomatic: kept as printed.

Latin abbreviation, almost certainly 'i.e.' (id est): the 'i' (dotted) and the following point are clear; the second glyph reads as a tall stroke and is ambiguous at 400 DPI (could be 'e' or 'l'). Read as 'e' on Latin convention and sense ('esteemed by tradition, i.e. Christ and his Apostles'). Low-medium confidence on the second glyph.
As-printed for 'abounding' (dropped 'o') — archaic variant / printer slip. Confirmed at 4x. Kept diplomatically.

Intended word is 'confutation'. The medial glyph was adjudicated at 5x against the adjacent short crossbarred 't' in 'correction' and in the '-ation' suffix on the same line: it clearly descends below the baseline and has NO crossbar = a LONG-ſ, not a 't'. So the compositor set a long-ſ sort where 't' was intended. Kept as printed 'confuſation' (glyph-driven, per §long-ſ).
As-printed for 'foundation' (dropped 'o') — archaic variant. Kept diplomatically.

This final line of p.19 shifts to genuine gapped 'vv': 'lavv', 'Likevviſe', 'vvhat' are unambiguous two-stroke vv (verified 3.5x), and 'VVhat' is a gapped capital VV. 'written' here reads as two strokes but with a less-distinct gap than its neighbours — transcribed 'vvritten' to match the line's vv regime (w-sort likely ran short at page foot). Borderline; could be a connected 'written'. Medium confidence. Rest of the body (both pages) uses connected real 'w'.

The expected 'of' ('casting out OF Paradise') is NOT printed: line_index 48 ends with 'out' flush to the right margin (verified 5x) and line_index 49 begins 'Paradiſe' (with French spacing 'Paradiſe ,'). Transcribed diplomatically WITHOUT inserting 'of'.
Left-margin citation cluster (p.19), small roman type near the 400 DPI limit. Book names read confidently; chapter digits read but medium confidence (esp. 'Iacob. 2.' — 1 vs 2 ambiguous).

Right-margin gloss (p.19) reads 'from Noe to their ſonnes of Iſrael' — the token before 'ſonnes' is letters 'their' (verified 2.8x), NOT the digits 'the 12.'; slightly loose phrasing but glyph-driven read.

Word-initial/display CAPITALS use gapped 'VV': VVho (l16), VVherfore (l27), and margin VVhy/VVhat (m19-right-2). Right-margin roman glosses (p.19) use connected 'w' (written, was, Alwayes, knowen) with display-initial gapped VV. Counts: 4 lowercase 'vv', 5 'VV'.

'confuſation' (l14) IS a long-ſ (see uncertain). ſt and ſh appear as tied ligatures where set; transcribed as component letters (ſ+t, ſ+h) per §glyph-repertoire.

method: Visual-multimodal read of the 400 DPI jp2 rasters (scan pp.19-20 of archive-ot1-1609), region-cropped and zoomed 2.5x-6x per line/word for diplomatic glyph decisions (long-ſ, w/vv, ligatures, typos). No OCR scaffold used. VALIDATION: (1) Localization — identified by the p.19 display heading 'THE ARGVMENT OF THE BOOKE OF GENESIS.' + the p.20 running header 'THE ARGVMENT OF GENESIS.' + content (the argument of Genesis, dividing the book into eight parts); it follows 'Of Moyses' and precedes 'The ſignification of the markes', exactly as briefed. (2) Identity — 1609 OT1 (First Tome): the volume's Approbatio is dated 'Duaci. 8. Nouembris. 1609', and this is the standard Douay-OT-Tome-1 front-matter Argument. (3) Placement — scan pages 19-20; no printed folio on either page (the Argument sits on the last preliminary leaf; printed foliation begins 'I' on scan p.21 = Genesis chap. 1, running header 'Creation.'); modern pencil foliation '16'/'17' in top-right corners. (4) Completeness — WHOLE section captured: opens p.19 (drop-cap 'THIS firſt Booke...'), carries across the leaf-turn via catchword 'maner,' → p.20 'maner, Iacob...', and ends p.20 at 'death. in the fiue laſt cahpters.' immediately above the next section 'The ſignification of the markes here vſed, for direction of the reader.' (excluded). p.21 begins Genesis chap. 1 proper. NOTE: French spacing before high punctuation (: ; ? !) is present in this fount but was not exhaustively adjudicated at 400 DPI; punctuation transcribed mostly tight — flag for a French-spacing review pass.
confidence: HIGH on localization, identity, placement, completeness, the two-line heading, the p.20 running header, and the bulk of both paragraphs and marginalia. HIGH (as-printed) on the six preserved typos (Sripture, abunding, confuſation, fundation, trangreſſion, cahpters) — each verified at high zoom. MEDIUM on: the 'i.⟨e?⟩' abbreviation (2nd glyph), the line_index 40 'vvritten' w/vv borderline, small left-margin citation digits, and the Augustine abbreviation 'queſt. vet'. LOW-confidence items are all flagged in uncertain[].
